note: Every rule below is fixed HERE, before a single record of test #4 was collected. Committed in its own commit, ahead of the collection commit and ahead of the evaluation commit, so the ordering is provable from git history rather than asserted. This is the same device the P6.27 country declaration used, and it is used again because it is the only part of the design that a reader cannot be asked to take on trust.

candidateFrozenFirst.note: The candidate, its corpus, its features, its hyperparameters, its seed, its threshold and the ship/reject rule were frozen and pushed BEFORE this declaration, and therefore before the test exists. Nothing about the model can be tuned to this instrument because the instrument was not built when the model was fixed.

universe.rule: IDENTICAL to the P6.27 declaration. Not one country is added, removed or reordered. The list is reused verbatim precisely so that no country selection happens in this phase at all - there is no choice left to make, and therefore none that could have been made against a result.
universe.selectionCriterion: Availability and breadth only, as declared in P6.27: every country any prior CIPHER collection has queried, plus every additional country measured to hold at least one LEI-bearing business entity. Explicitly NOT chosen by expected cross-border density, legal-form density, or anything either model was observed to do.

sources.name: Wikidata
sources.role: anchor - every positive pair has a Wikidata side

sources.name: GLEIF
sources.role: LEI counterpart, derived from the LEIs Wikidata publishes

sources.name: SEC EDGAR
sources.role: CIK counterpart, derived from the CIKs Wikidata publishes

universe.sourceRule: The adapter set is the allowlist and it is unchanged. No source is added for this test and no source is dropped from it, so there is no post-hoc source selection either.

collectionRule.query: The same constant country-scoped query as test #3 (src/lib/adapters/public/wikidata.ts, countryQuery). No predicate is added, removed or reweighted.
collectionRule.pageSizeUnit: SPARQL result ROWS, which is the adapter's MAX_LIMIT
collectionRule.orderingRationale: Two measured facts mean test #3's single LIMIT 2000 page did not take everything the publisher returns for a country of any size. (1) The property path wdt:P31/wdt:P279* emits one row per derivation and the OPTIONAL enrichments cross-multiply on top, so 2,000 rows yielded 521 distinct items for CZ and 280 for US; the row limit binds far below the item count. (2) LIMIT without ORDER BY returns an arbitrary subset and SPARQL guarantees nothing about which, so re-running is not a way to reach the rest. Ascending QID is publisher-assigned creation order: content-blind, stable, and unrelated to name, jurisdiction mix, or anything either model was observed to do.
collectionRule.earlyStop: stop paging a country as soon as a page returns fewer than 2000 rows - that country is exhausted
collectionRule.uniformity: The page cap is the SAME for all 108 countries. No country is given more pages than another, so the jurisdiction mix of the result is decided by what the publisher holds and not by the experimenter.
collectionRule.withinCountrySelection: NONE. Every row a page returns is kept.
collectionRule.gleifRule: Every LEI that survives the freshness filter below, and no others, resolved through --leis-from in bounded chunks of the adapter's MAX_LIMIT (500). The LEI set is derived from the collected Wikidata records, never hand-typed and never crawled.
collectionRule.edgarRule: Every CIK that survives the freshness filter, resolved through --ciks-from from the same collected Wikidata records.

splitRule.rule: ONE partition. Nothing in test #4 is ever fitted on, so a train/validation cut would only invite someone to fit on it later. Built with --all-test, as tests #1, #2 and #3 were.
splitRule.subjectBucket: NONE. P6.27 halved its pool by sha256(seed|subject) because that sweep had to yield both a test and a training corpus. This sweep yields only a test - v4 already exists and is the training half - so the whole fresh pool is the test and no hash split is applied.

seeds.note: Names the dataset build; with --all-test it selects no partition, and is recorded so the build is reproducible.

freshnessRule.unit: subject - the LEI or CIK, which is the unit the split policy and leakage checks L1-L13 operate on
freshnessRule.enforcement: at corpus-build time, at the RECORD level, before a single pair is formed
freshnessRule.note: ALL SEVEN prior datasets, in EVERY partition. A subject seen in v1's train is as disqualifying as one seen in test #3. This is stricter than test #3's rule only in that there are now two more datasets to exclude; the rule itself is unchanged. The P6.16 no-identifier pilot's reserved LEIs are excluded as well, as in every prior frozen test.
freshnessRule.noPriorInspection: No record of test #4 has been read, scored, or inspected by a human for model tuning, and none may be before both models are scored. The availability census that established this test is buildable at all counted LEI-bearing items per country and read no entity name.

subjects.note: test #3 held 2,812 subjects; a materially smaller instrument would not support the cross-border and legal-form breakdowns this decision needs

targetSize.insufficientDataRule: If the collection cannot reach the minimum from genuinely fresh subjects, the outcome is BLOCKED. The freshness rule is NOT weakened to obtain a result, the country list is NOT extended to chase yield, and no prior test is re-used.

leakageRule.requirement: PASS on every check before either model is scored
leakageRule.L13Requirement: 0 subjects in this test fitted on by any earlier build; anything above 0 blocks scoring

evaluationProtocol.thresholds: each model at its own frozen threshold, fixed before collection and recorded above
evaluationProtocol.decisionRule: docs/evaluation/ml-selection-freeze-e2.md section 3, carried forward unchanged from the P6.27 freeze
requiredBreakdowns: unrelated entities sharing generic or legal-form language
validation-to-test false-merge inflation factor for both models
evaluationProtocol.aggregateAloneForbidden: The aggregate is never reported alone, and F1 is not the criterion. A false merge fuses two real companies into one node and every downstream inference inherits it; a miss leaves two nodes a human can still join.
evaluationProtocol.failureInspection: representative FP/FN failures inspected only AFTER the metrics are fixed and recorded
evaluationProtocol.tuningForbidden: E2 must not be tuned, re-thresholded, re-trained or patched in response to anything test #4 says - including the Latvian legal-form behaviour it is pre-registered to measure.

afterThisTest.rule: This is intended to be the final P6 model-selection experiment. SHIP E2 closes ML training; KEEP V2 closes ML training; BLOCKED stops and reports. No further candidate is started unless a reproducibility or correctness defect invalidates this experiment itself.
afterThisTest.testStatusAfterScoring: SPENT - scored once, used to decide, never again quotable as unseen
